rationale: The assistant correctly identified the start relay/overload as the most likely cause, with the compressor as the alternative, and kept to safe unplugged checks. It escalated to an engineer at the right point and gave sensible food-protection advice. It did not suggest a specific part purchase. Minor gaps: it did not mention the model-specific relay swap option or the repair-cost economics against the customer's budget, and the second reply partly repeated the interim advice from the first. The 'burnt smell' check was reasonable, though the customer had already said there was no burning smell.
